chunks: Abdul Wahid narrated through his chain, from al-Hasan, from Hafs bin Naseeb Far'an who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) during the days when his mawla al-Mu'alla bin Khunays was killed. He said to me: 'O Hafs! I told al-Mu'alla some things, so he spread them, and he was afflicted with the iron (of execution). Indeed, I said to him: We have a tradition; whoever preserves it for us, Allah will preserve his religion and his worldly life, and whoever spreads it for us, Allah will deprive him of his religion and his worldly life. O Mu'alla! Indeed, whoever conceals the difficult (challenging) parts of our tradition, Allah will make it a light between his eyes and grant him honor among the people, and whoever spreads the difficult parts of our tradition, he will not die until a weapon bites him or he dies confused.'

key_terms.الصَّعْب: The difficult/challenging parts of the traditions, often referring to esoteric or secret knowledge
key_terms.الْحَدِيد: Iron, referring to execution by sword or beheading
key_terms.الْمُعَلَّى بْنِ خُنَيْسَ: Al-Mu'alla bin Khunays, a companion and mawla of Imam al-Sad
key_terms.نُورًا بَيْنَ عَيْنَيْهِ: A light between his eyes, a metaphor for clarity and insight

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of spreading the secret traditions of the Imams according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the critical Shia concept of *taqiyya* and the strategic preservation of esoteric knowledge (*al-sa'b*) during periods of political persecution, specifically referencing the execution of al-Mu'alla bin Khunays. The Imam establishes a divine correlation between concealing difficult traditions and receiving spiritual light (*nur*) and worldly honor, whereas public dissemination leads to the loss of both faith and life, often through martyrdom or confusion.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (12) Abdul Wahid narrated from al-Hasan that Hafs bin Naseeb Far’an had said: “I came to Abu Abdullah (as) when his mawla al-Mu’alla bin Khunays was killed.

He said to me: “O Hafs, I have told al-Mu’alla of some things but he spread them then he was afflicted with (iron). I have said to him: We have some traditions, which if someone keeps secret Allah will save his religion and life and if he spreads, Allah will deprive him of his religion and life. O Mu’alla, if one hides the serious traditions of ours, Allah will make that as light between his eyes and grant him with glory among people and if one spreads the serious traditions of ours, he will not die until he is bitten by weapon or he dies confusedly.”
